name: Sheep View 360 (#wewantgooglestreetview)
objective: Pressure Google into adding the Faroe Islands to Google Street View and raise global awareness of the islands.
insight: The Faroe Islands were missing from Google Street View, making the destination hard to discover and explore online.
creative_idea: If Google won't map the islands, the islands' sheep will: 'Sheep View 360'.
execution: Visit Faroe Islands' Durita Dahl Andreassen fitted sheep with solar-powered 360-degree cameras; images were geotagged and uploaded to Street View, supported by a #wewantgooglestreetview social push and petition.
participation_mechanism: Public invited to support the #wewantgooglestreetview hashtag/petition and explore the sheep-captured imagery online.
target_audience: Global online audience and prospective travellers; Google as the 'target' of the stunt.

sources.title: Faroe Islands Lack Google Street View, But They Have 'Sheep View 360'
Sheep View: Faroe Islands Captured for Google by Four-Legged Crew
Thanks to Sheep View, the Faroe Islands now has Google Street View

published_results: Visit Faroe Islands states that Google announced Street View now features the Faroe Islands; per coverage, Google supplied a Street View Trekker and 360-degree cameras via its camera loan programme (reported by Visit Faroe Islands and WebUrbanist).
strategic_learning: Interpretation: A tiny budget can earn global reach when the stunt picks a famous 'opponent' (Google), has a clear ask, and a visual absurdity (sheep with cameras) that media can retell in one line.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Scapia could frame a playful public 'ask' to a big platform or airline (e.g. a missing route) and let users rally behind it with a hashtag, turning a product gap into earned media.

name: Closed for Maintenance, Open for Voluntourism
objective: Protect fragile, popular natural sites from tourism wear while generating positive global attention for responsible tourism.
insight: Rising visitor numbers were damaging popular sites; the board reframed the problem as an invitation to help care for the islands.
creative_idea: Officially 'close' the islands' popular sites for a weekend of maintenance, and open them only to volunteer tourists who help repair them.
execution: Popular tourist sites were closed for a weekend in late April 2019 (around 26-27 April); 100 international volunteers from 25 countries, chosen from about 3,500 applicants, worked on trail and site maintenance with free accommodation and food (paying their own flights). The initiative has been repeated in later years.
participation_mechanism: Open online application for volunteer places; selected volunteers participate in on-ground maintenance projects.
target_audience: Responsible, nature-loving international travellers; global media.

sources.title: Faroe Islands closes to tourists except for volunteers
Faroe Islands closed to tourists
Why close the Faroe Islands for maintenance

published_results: Coverage reported 100 volunteers from 25 countries chosen from about 3,500 applicants in 2019 (weather.com, Business Insider). Visit Faroe Islands' facts page (as surfaced in search, 2024 figures) lists 54 projects on 10 islands, 23,806 applicants, 409 foreign and 202 Faroese volunteers. A Cannes/Eurobest case entry claims locals' favourable view of tourism rose from 56% to 71% (self-reported award entry).
strategic_learning: Interpretation: Turning a constraint (overtourism) into scarcity and purpose ('closed' + volunteers only) generates far more interest than a standard 'visit us' message, and positions the brand as responsible.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Limited-seat, purpose-led trips (e.g. a 'clean-up weekend' at an Indian hill station co-funded with card rewards) can create earned media and brand affinity with conscious travellers.

name: The Swedish Number
objective: Promote Sweden and Swedish openness/free speech, marking the 250th anniversary of Sweden's abolition of censorship.
insight: The most credible ambassadors for Sweden are ordinary Swedes themselves.
creative_idea: Give Sweden its own phone number: anyone in the world can call and be connected to a random Swede.
execution: A dedicated number (+46 771 793 336) routed calls to Swedes who had downloaded an app to volunteer as ambassadors; ran from 6 April to 25 July 2016. Created by INGO Stockholm (WPP). Note: Visit Sweden was involved early but left development before launch.
participation_mechanism: Global public calls the number; Swedes opt in via app to answer calls.
target_audience: Global curious public and prospective visitors; Swedish citizens as volunteer ambassadors.

sources.title: The Swedish Number
Cannes Lions: The Swedish Number
Cannes Lions 2016 Direct Lions Grand Prix

published_results: Bizcommunity reported it won the Direct Lions Grand Prix at Cannes Lions 2016. A WPP awards page reports nearly 190,000 calls from 186 countries; Wikipedia cites 197,678 calls.
strategic_learning: Interpretation: Handing the brand voice to real locals in a live, unscripted channel creates authenticity and talkability that scripted ads cannot.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: A 'call/chat a local' mechanic (e.g. Scapia cardholders who live in a destination answering questions from travellers) could build community and trust around trip planning.

name: Rent a Finn
objective: Increase interest in, and tourism to, Finland by leveraging its status as the world's happiest country.
insight: Finland had been named the happiest country in the UN World Happiness Report, but happiness is best explained by living it with Finns, often through nature.
creative_idea: 'Rent' a local Finn as a happiness guide who shares their everyday, nature-based way of life.
execution: Eight Finnish 'happiness guides' hosted selected visitors for three days of activities (e.g. fishing, berry picking, sauna) in summer 2019. Created with agency SEK (Grey). A virtual follow-up, 'Rent a Finn goes Virtual', ran in 2020.
participation_mechanism: Travellers applied by submitting short videos (deadline reported as 14 April 2019); Finns applied to become guides.
target_audience: International travellers seeking wellbeing, nature and authentic local experiences.

sources.title: Visit Finland: Rent a Finn
Finland's New Tourism Campaign Wants to Show You Why It's the Happiest Country in the World
Rent a Finn seeks to capitalise on UN happiness recognition

published_results: Ads of the World (agency case) states reach in 149 countries with paid media in only 10 markets, ~98.5% of reach from earned media, a ~EUR 200K communications budget, and PR value of EUR 34,175,321. Early coverage reported 755 video applications from 78 countries. These are largely agency-reported figures.
strategic_learning: Interpretation: Converting an abstract third-party accolade (happiest country) into a tangible, human experience gives media a concrete story and makes the claim believable.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Scapia could turn a destination's 'known for' attribute into a hosted, contest-style experience with real locals, using UGC video entries to drive engagement.

name: Come and Say G'day (global launch, Ruby the Roo)
objective: Re-ignite international demand for Australia after border reopening; Tourism Australia's first global campaign since 2016.
insight: Australia needed a warm, distinctive, unashamedly Australian invitation that could be localised across many markets.
creative_idea: Ruby, a CGI souvenir kangaroo, becomes Australia's ambassador and invites the world to 'come and say g'day'.
execution: Teased via billboards in Tokyo, Singapore, London and New York before an official launch on 19 October 2022 with the animated short film 'G'day' (M&C Saatchi; NBCUniversal partnership mirroring a film release). Ruby was voiced by Rose Byrne in English markets and localised in others.
participation_mechanism: Primarily broadcast/brand; audiences engage with the film and character across social and OOH.
target_audience: High-value international travellers across 15 global markets (media spend in nine).

sources.title: Tourism Australia Teases New Global 'Come & Say G'day' Campaign Via M&C Saatchi
Tourism Australia's 'Ruby the Roo' TV ad revealed
'Ruby the Roo is off to a flying start!': Industry responds to TA's new campaign

published_results: B&T reported Australia was up 12 percentage points in consideration, 13 points in intention to travel and 10 points in share of search (baseline/period not stated). Tourism Australia's managing director said share of flight search was up 10% globally vs 2019. An agency case study claims 650M+ views and $193M+ earned media (agency-reported).
strategic_learning: Interpretation: A ownable character (Ruby) acts as a flexible brand asset that can be re-cast with local celebrities per market, giving global consistency plus local relevance.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: A recurring mascot/character platform can let Scapia run many destination- or season-specific stories while keeping one recognisable brand device.

name: OutHorse Your Email
objective: Encourage travellers to switch off and holiday in Iceland, driving consideration in key markets.
insight: Visit Iceland's survey found 55% of respondents check work email at least once a day on holiday.
creative_idea: Let Icelandic horses answer your work email while you're on holiday in Iceland.
execution: Three real horses (Litla Stjarna, Hekla, Hrímnir) 'typed' replies on a giant keyboard; users picked a horse and got an out-of-office message, supported by a campaign video.
participation_mechanism: Users choose a horse on the website, enter name/email/return date and receive an auto-reply/out-of-office to set up.
target_audience: Overworked professionals in markets such as the US and Germany.

sources.title: Iceland Invites You To 'Outhorse' Your Emails
Iceland tourism ad invites you to 'outhorse' your work emails while visiting
Visit Iceland: OutHorse your email (SABRE Awards)

published_results: AFP (via Dawn) reported about 8,000 sign-ups early on. WARC's SABRE Awards case reports US$6.8m earned media and consideration of a trip to Iceland up 16.8% in the US and 12.2% in Germany (agency-submitted figures).
strategic_learning: Interpretation: Anchoring a whimsical mechanic in a genuine, data-backed pain point (always-on work culture) makes the stunt feel useful and shareable rather than random.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Indian professionals' 'can't switch off' pain point could power a utility-plus-humour mechanic (e.g. a Scapia out-of-office generator tied to a trip booking).

name: Good Morning World (100% Pure Welcome)
objective: Extend the 100% Pure New Zealand brand with a warm, people-led welcome to the world.
insight: New Zealand is among the first places to see the sun each day, so it can literally say 'good morning' to the world first.
creative_idea: Every day for a year, a different New Zealander greets the world from their own sunrise.
execution: Daily sunrise welcome videos from locals posted on Instagram (@goodmorningworldnz), launched with a feature film at Hikurangi, Gisborne; Special Group was the agency, with Australia leading rollout across TV, cinema, OOH, YouTube, Facebook and Instagram.
participation_mechanism: 300+ New Zealanders contributed greetings; global viewers commented and replied with their own 'good mornings'.
target_audience: Global prospective travellers, starting with Australia.

sources.title: Tourism NZ says 'Good Morning World' in global 100% Pure Welcome campaign via Special Group
The sun rises on a world first welcome from New Zealand
Tourism NZ marks 100 days of Good Morning World series

published_results: Special Group's own case study claims 605M+ global impressions, 12M+ likes and comments, a 1,590% rise in searches for 'New Zealand' and greetings from 60+ countries (agency-reported, not independently verified).
strategic_learning: Interpretation: An always-on, daily serialised format with a simple ritual builds habit and repeat exposure on social at low production cost per episode.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: A daily 'postcard from a Scapia member' series could build an always-on UGC content engine and community ritual.

name: Discover the Originals
objective: Invite the world to discover the whole of Sweden, including lesser-known places.
insight: Many IKEA product names are real Swedish places, yet searching those names returns furniture rather than the destinations.
creative_idea: Reclaim IKEA product names by showing the original places behind them.
execution: Forsman & Bodenfors matched 21 popular IKEA products to their namesake towns, lakes and mountains (e.g. Lake Bolmen, 'more than an IKEA toilet brush') with humorous content.
participation_mechanism: Audiences explore an online catalogue-style showcase of the 'originals' behind product names.

sources.title: Visit Sweden campaign reveals the tourism gems behind Ikea product names
Sweden tourism campaign reclaims IKEA names
Sweden's tourist campaign highlights the places IKEA products are named after

strategic_learning: Interpretation: Borrowing familiarity from a globally known brand gives obscure places instant recognition and makes dispersal to lesser-known regions feel fun rather than dutiful.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Scapia could use familiar cultural references (film locations, brand or dish names) as a hook to push travellers towards underexplored destinations.

name: Land of Everyday Wonder: AI-powered landmarks ('Don't come to see me - visit Denmark')
objective: Build interest in Denmark as an alternative to crowded bucket-list sights, under the 'Land of Everyday Wonder' brand.
insight: YouGov research commissioned by VisitDenmark (Nov 2022) found over half of respondents in the UK, Germany and Sweden felt overcrowded sites made holidays disappointing.
creative_idea: Famous landmarks and artworks (Mona Lisa, Statue of Liberty, Girl with a Pearl Earring) themselves tell people not to queue for them, and to visit Denmark instead.
execution: Deepfake/motion-synthesis films with AI-written scripts (lightly edited by VisitDenmark), by Brandhouse/Subsero; the 62-second hero film shows Denmark for only 11 seconds.
target_audience: Travellers in markets including the UK, US, Germany and Sweden who are tired of crowds.

sources.title: AI-Powered Foreign Tourist Sites Playfully Extol Denmark's Virtues in Innovative Marketing Campaign
VisitDenmark launches truly bonkers deepfake ad written entirely by AI
Mona Lisa and AI team up to lead Danish tourism push

strategic_learning: Interpretation: Positioning against overtourism by letting competitors' icons 'endorse' you is a sharp challenger move; early use of generative AI added news value.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: A challenger frame ('skip the crowded hotspot, try X') could help Scapia promote alternative Indian or Asian destinations, and timely tech (AI) can itself be the PR hook.

name: #BeMyGuest with Shah Rukh Khan
tourism_board: Dubai Tourism (Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism)
objective: Attract more Indian travellers to Dubai; India described by Dubai Tourism as a key source market.
insight: Shah Rukh Khan has enormous appeal with Indian audiences and a long association with Dubai.
creative_idea: Shah Rukh Khan plays host, inviting audiences to be his guest in Dubai.
execution: First film released 10 December 2016 (Nirvana Films, directed by Prakash Varma) after Facebook teasers; sequels followed, including Kabir Khan-directed short films (2018) and a six-part treasure-hunt series (from 25 February 2019).
participation_mechanism: Viewing/sharing of film series on social; treasure-hunt format in the 2019 series.

sources.title: Over 5.7 million views in 5 days: Is this really a tourism ad?
Indian actor Shah Rukh Khan again features in Dubai Tourism ad campaign
Shah Rukh Khan Be My Guest campaign (press release)
sources.publisher: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism

published_results: afaqs headline reported over 5.7 million views in five days for the first film. Later coverage cited Dubai Tourism figures of 45 million views and 65 million engagements for the first film, and over 100 million views worldwide for the 2017 sequel (Dubai Tourism, via Gulf Business/Arabian Business).
strategic_learning: Interpretation: A superstar with authentic affinity for the destination, in a serialised host format, sustains interest across years rather than a single burst.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: For Indian audiences, a credible celebrity 'host' in an episodic series can carry a destination or product story far longer than one-off ads.

name: Neeraj Chopra as Switzerland Tourism 'Friendship Ambassador' (India)
objective: Showcase the sporty, outdoor and adventurous side of Switzerland to Indian travellers.
insight: Post-COVID, more Indians value being outdoors and active; India is a very important long-haul market for Switzerland (per Switzerland Tourism India director Misha Gambetta).
creative_idea: Olympic gold medallist Neeraj Chopra, an outdoorsy Indian icon, becomes Switzerland's Friendship Ambassador.
execution: Chopra visited destinations including Interlaken, Zermatt and Geneva and shares experiences of snow sports, hiking, biking and adventure activities.
participation_mechanism: Ambassador-led content; no audience mechanic reported.
target_audience: Indian travellers interested in outdoor and adventure experiences.

sources.title: Neeraj Chopra is the 'Friendship Ambassador' of Switzerland
Switzerland Has A New Friendship Ambassador

strategic_learning: Interpretation: Choosing an ambassador who embodies the specific positioning being pushed (active/adventure rather than romance/Bollywood) helps reposition a destination many Indians already know.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Scapia can pick ambassadors/creators to shift perception of a known destination toward a new use-case (e.g. adventure Europe vs honeymoon Europe).

name: Howzat for a Holiday? (Pat Cummins x Ruby, India)
objective: Attract high-potential Indian travellers by riding the 2024-25 Australia-India Test cricket series.
insight: Indian cricket fans would be watching Australia on screen for weeks during the series; cricket is a natural bridge between the two countries.
creative_idea: Australian Test captain Pat Cummins teams up with Ruby the Kangaroo to show Indian fans holiday experiences beyond the cricket field.
execution: Launched 21 November 2024 ahead of the first Test in Perth; TVC (30, 15 and 6-second cuts) shows the MCG, Cape Tribulation, Kangaroo Island, Rottnest Island and beach cricket at Palm Beach, plus OOH and digital in India. Agency: The Monkeys. Part of the 'Come and Say G'day' platform.
participation_mechanism: None reported; media placed during match broadcasts.
target_audience: Indian cricket fans and high-potential Indian travellers.

sources.title: Howzat for a holiday? Australia appeals to Indian tourists ahead of Test cricket series
sources.publisher: Minister for Trade and Tourism, Australian Government

sources.title: Pat Cummins stars in Tourism Australia's new 'Come and Say G'day' ad
Cricketer Pat Cummins stars in Tourism Australia's Come and Say G'day campaign to run in India via The Monkeys

published_results: No post-campaign results found. Launch coverage cited an expected audience of up to 50 million Indian viewers (projection, not a result).
strategic_learning: Interpretation: Tying media to a high-attention, time-bound cultural moment (a Test series) concentrates reach among an audience already primed to think about the destination.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Scapia could build moment-based travel offers around India-abroad cricket tours or other events, timed to broadcasts when interest in the host country peaks.

name: Come and Say G'day - India chapter with Sara Tendulkar
objective: Grow Indian arrivals as part of the second chapter of the global Come and Say G'day campaign (reported target of half a million Indian visitors a year, per afaqs).
insight: Tourism Australia said it wanted to show Australian holidays through the eyes of visitors from India, with creative tailored to Indian cultural nuances, rather than adapting one global ad.
creative_idea: Ruby the Souvenir Kangaroo returns, joined by Sara Tendulkar, in bespoke India creative.
execution: Launched in India on 20 August 2025, after the global second chapter began in China on 7 August; other markets used local talent (e.g. Robert Irwin, Nigella Lawson). Reported as part of a A$130 million phase.
target_audience: Indian travellers; India is reported as Australia's fifth-largest visitor source market.

sources.title: Tourism Australia launches new Come and Say G'day campaign targeting Indian travellers starring Sara Tendulkar
With Sara Tendulkar onboard, Tourism Australia eyes half a million Indian visitors a year
Sara Tendulkar stars in Tourism Australia's Come and Say G'day campaign in India

strategic_learning: Interpretation: Moving from one adapted global ad to bespoke market creative with a local face signals that India is now a priority market and improves cultural fit.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Co-marketing with boards that build India-specific creative is an opportunity; Scapia can attach card offers/booking flows to these high-visibility pushes.

name: #BeyondTheFilter with Rajkummar Rao and Patralekhaa
objective: Inspire Indian travellers to experience New Zealand authentically, beyond scenic, filtered imagery.
insight: Heavily filtered social media travel content sets up expectations; genuine, present-moment experiences are what make New Zealand special.
creative_idea: Real-life couple Rajkummar Rao and Patralekhaa experience New Zealand as themselves, 'beyond the filter'.
execution: Short-film mini-series (described by one outlet as five parts) shot across the North Island, including Sanctuary Mountain, Auckland's coastal waters, Taupō and The Haka Shop; directed by Navzar Eranee and Shankar Raman; rolled out in phases on Tourism New Zealand's India site and owned channels plus paid digital/social.
target_audience: Indian travellers, particularly couples seeking authentic experiences.

sources.title: Tourism New Zealand launches #BeyondTheFilter campaign with Rajkummar Rao and Patralekhaa as brand advocates
Tourism New Zealand drops #BeyondTheFilter mini-series starring Rajkummar Rao and Patralekhaa
Tourism agency enlists Bollywood couple to woo Indian tourists

published_results: The agency reported its Mumbai launch event drew 33 media outlets and 379 million reach (agency-reported, as surfaced in search results; not independently verified).
strategic_learning: Interpretation: An 'anti-filter' authenticity message plus a real couple gives a fresh angle in a category saturated with polished influencer content.
scapia_relevance: Interpretation: Scapia's creator content could lean into unpolished, real-traveller storytelling to stand out from glossy travel influencer feeds.
